hypothesis: For eligible known-mapping continuous-control switches, conditioning the receiver from the fresh actually-applied actuator input reduces first-output command discontinuity by >=25% versus cold-start, without violating fencing/release gates or worsening the safety bound.
corner_case: saturation-at-switch: record behavior; require no state bound violation, do not count toward efficacy margin because shared saturation can mask raw differences
plant: scalar discrete plant y_next=y+0.25*(u-y); reference=1; output clamp [0,1]; actuator slew <=0.2/tick; receiver proportional gain 2.0 and held integrator offset initialized z=applied_u-2*(reference-y); horizon 20 ticks
controls: two-tick handoff delay with no receiver output before source quiescence acknowledgement
mutation controls for stale-state acceptance, early receiver actuation, and conditioning from requested instead of applied input
decision: METHOD_PASS_SCOPED only if both eligible cases improve discontinuity by >=25%, saturation safety bound y<=1.0 holds, every denied control has zero receiver actuation, delayed handoff waits for quiescence before exactly one receiver actuation, and all three mutation controls are detected; otherwise FAIL/HOLD per failure locus.
counterhypothesis: cold start may track faster; saturation may hide discontinuity; a lower first-output jump may worsen task performance; synthetic plant transfer may fail.
uncertainty: No real backend, noisy/delayed sensor, model planner, semantics, GUI/game dynamics, or physical input. Not runtime evidence.
execution: WSLc CPU-only one container; pinned cached image; no network; source read-only; separate output; cpu=1; memory=256m (limit enforcement not established)
